name: AR-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Steve Womack defends a district with a 13-point Republican lean
Fundraising gap: Womack has $2.4M on hand versus about $16K for Robb Ryerse
Polymarket prices a Democratic win at roughly 3%
No public polls or expert ratings; Libertarian Bobby Wilson on the ballot shaves Womack's margin slightly
model.rationale: The district's 13-point Republican lean, Womack's incumbency advantage, and a roughly fifteen-to-one fundraising edge leave little evidence of a competitive race, and prediction markets agree at about a 3 percent Democratic chance. Even a national environment tilted toward Democrats does not close a gap this wide.
model.watch: Only a historic wave environment for Democrats, combined with unexpected polling showing a genuine contest, would move this from Safe Republican toward a competitive rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Arkansas's third district is a solidly Republican seat, and Steve Womack holds it as the incumbent seeking another term. He enters the general election with about $2.4 million on hand, while Democrat Robb Ryerse has raised roughly $159,000 and reports about $16,000 in cash. No public polling or expert ratings are available for the race, so expectations rest on the district's Republican-leaning fundamentals and the money gap. Libertarian Bobby Wilson also appears on the ballot.

Prediction markets give Ryerse roughly a 3 percent chance of winning, and the district's partisan lean of about 13 points Republican makes a serious challenge unlikely even in an environment that favors Democrats. With no polling, no outside spending, and a fifteen-to-one fundraising gap, there are few signs of a competitive race. The seat is rated Safe Republican, with an expected margin near 16 points.
